title: LangSmith Self-Hosted Health
description: Operator view of a self-hosted LangSmith installation with SmithDB: data loss, backlogs, failures, and infrastructure saturation. Version 2026-11-25.

definition.content:
## LangSmith self-hosted health
This dashboard answers one question: **are all components healthy?** It is for SmithDB in cluster mode (`smithdb.topology: cluster`, the default). **Version 2026-11-25.** To update, import the newest version into this dashboard (Configure, Import dashboard JSON).

**Use it.** Select your installation with **env**, **cluster**, and **namespace**. Then select your resources with **redis** and **metastore**. Each takes one tag of the resource, for example `cluster_id:<name>` for Memorystore for Redis Cluster, `cacheclusterid:<node>` for ElastiCache, `dbclusteridentifier:<name>` for Aurora, or `database_id:<project>:<name>` for Cloud SQL. The lines of the other cloud providers then stay empty, and resources of other applications are not shown. Start with the tiles at the top. **Load** shows the work that comes in. **Health** turns yellow or red when an area needs attention. Open the section that the tile names. Each component section shows **Service metrics** first, and **Infrastructure** below. The info icon of each chart tells what it measures, why it matters, what to do, and which data it needs. Dashed lines mark thresholds: yellow for a warning, red for critical or a hard limit.

**Collect the data** ([guide](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-observability-dashboards)). SmithDB metrics are queried under the `smithdb.` prefix. Configure your collector to match. `langsmith_*` metrics carry no prefix. Optional: one line of *Failed queries by cause* uses a SmithDB metric that the Helm chart does not export by default. To fill it, set `SMITHDB_<COMPONENT>__METRICS__MODE` to `all`, for example in `smithdb.commonEnv`. Its tooltip says so. The example configuration also collects the LangSmith metrics that this dashboard needs, from the platform backend and the ingest queue. If you use your own configuration, add them to the OpenMetrics `metrics` list of these services. The tooltips name them. Infrastructure charts need the Kubernetes integration. Redis and metastore charts need the Redis, PostgreSQL, or cloud provider integrations.

**Alerts and diagnosis.** [Recommended SmithDB alerts](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts) gives the monitor conditions. Each Health tile and each section links to its alerts. [Diagnose common SmithDB issues](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-common-issues) explains causes and fixes.

**How SmithDB works.** The [SmithDB guide](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb) explains the components and how data moves between them.

Green: no action. Yellow: examine soon. Red: act now. The tooltip of each tile gives its thresholds and the section to open. A tile that shows **No data** does not get the data it needs. The thresholds are starting values. Adjust them to your traffic. [Recommended SmithDB alerts](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts) · [SmithDB metrics reference](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-metrics)

#### Load
The work that reaches the system now. The Workload section shows the trends.

definition.title: Runs stored per second
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Runs that SmithDB stored successfully per second, averaged over the selected time range.

**Why it matters:** This is the main load figure. Backlogs and latency only make sense relative to it.

**What to do:** This tile has no thresholds. A sudden drop while clients still send traces means that ingestion fails; examine the Data loss and LangSmith ingestion sections.

**Requires:** LangSmith metrics from the platform backend or the ingest queue (`langsmith_ingestion_e2e_latency_seconds`). The example Datadog configuration collects them.

definition.title: Query requests per second
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Read requests to all SmithDB query pools per second, averaged over the selected time range. Feedback writes and deletes are not included.

**Why it matters:** This is the read load from the UI, the API, and automations.

**What to do:** This tile has no thresholds. If the value increases, examine query latency and failed queries in the SmithDB query section.

definition.content:
#### Health
Each tile turns yellow or red when its signal needs action.

definition.title: Data loss signals (should be 0)

formulas.formula: (default_zero(q1) + default_zero(q2) + default_zero(q3) + default_zero(q5) + default_zero(q4) + default_zero(q6) + default_zero(q7)) / (0 * g + 1)

definition.description:
**What it measures:** The sum of evictions of the Redis that you select with the redis variable (any provider), and ingestion tasks that failed their last attempt, during the selected time range. The last attempt is attempt 12 for run tasks and `persist_batched_feedbacks`, and attempt 25 for the feedback mutation tasks.

**Why it matters:** Each count can mean runs or feedback that SmithDB never stores. Users see missing traces or feedback.

**What to do:** Any value above 0 needs action. The tile shows No data until the LangSmith queue metrics are collected. If no Redis is selected, or its integration does not collect data, the Redis part counts as 0.

**Tile:** Green: 0. Red: above 0. Open the Data loss section. Matches [Alerts 1](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#1-runs-are-lost) and [2](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#2-feedback-is-lost). For a monitor, use the Redis evictions over the last 5 minutes, and the last-attempt failures over the last 15 minutes: attempt 12 for run tasks and `persist_batched_feedbacks`, attempt 25 for the feedback mutation tasks. Also warn on attempt 11 of `persist_batched_feedbacks`, because this task does not count all of its losses.

**Requires:** LangSmith metrics from the platform backend or the ingest queue (`langsmith_asynq_ingestion_queue_retry`, `langsmith_ingest_task_failures`). The example Datadog configuration collects them. One of the Redis integration, the ElastiCache integration, the Memorystore integration, or the Memorystore for Redis Cluster integration.

definition.title: Feedback at risk (should be 0)
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Failures of `persist_batched_feedbacks` at attempt 11, one attempt before its last, during the selected time range.

**Why it matters:** This task does not count a failure while the run of its feedback is not ingested yet. If its last attempt fails for this reason, the feedback is lost, but the Data loss tile does not show it. A failure at attempt 11 is often the last signal before the loss.

**What to do:** Above 0 means that feedback is probably lost. Examine the feedback chart in the Data loss section, and find the error in the logs of the ingest queue workers. If feedback fails often, set `smithdb.mutations.enabled: true`.

**Tile:** Green: 0. Yellow: above 0. Open the Data loss section. Matches the warning in [Alert 2](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#2-feedback-is-lost). For a monitor, use the same query over the last 15 minutes.

**Requires:** LangSmith metrics from the platform backend or the ingest queue (`langsmith_asynq_ingestion_queue_retry`, `langsmith_ingest_task_failures`). The example Datadog configuration collects them.

definition.title: Oldest waiting ingestion task
definition.description:
**What it measures:** The age of the oldest task in the ingestion queues that no ingest queue worker has started yet.

**Why it matters:** Run data in Redis expires after 6 hours by default (Helm value `config.settings.redisRunsExpirySeconds`). A task that waits longer loses its runs.

**What to do:** Normal is less than a few seconds, with short peaks of about 30 s. Warning above 10 minutes, critical above 30 minutes: workers cannot process tasks as fast as they arrive. Add ingest queue workers, or examine the SmithDB write latency.

**Tile:** Green: below 10 minutes. Yellow: 10 minutes or more. Red: 30 minutes or more. Open the LangSmith ingestion section. Matches [Alert 3](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#3-the-ingestion-backlog-gets-old). For a monitor, use the same query over the last 10 minutes.

**Requires:** LangSmith metrics from the platform backend or the ingest queue (`langsmith_asynq_queue_latency_seconds`). The example Datadog configuration collects them.

definition.title: Ingestion tasks waiting for retry
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Ingestion tasks whose write to SmithDB failed and that wait for their next attempt.

**Why it matters:** Failed writes are not visible to users until the last retry fails. After 12 retries (13 attempts, about 2.5 hours), the runs are lost.

**What to do:** Short peaks are normal. A value that stays high means that writes fail. Find the error in the logs of the ingest queue workers.

**Tile:** Green: below 100. Yellow: 100 or more. Red: 1,000 or more. Open the LangSmith ingestion section. Matches [Alert 3](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#3-the-ingestion-backlog-gets-old). For a monitor, use the same query, and alert when it stays above the threshold for the last 30 minutes.

**Requires:** LangSmith metrics from the platform backend or the ingest queue (`langsmith_asynq_ingestion_queue_retry`). The example Datadog configuration collects them.

definition.title: SmithDB write error rate
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Failed write calls to SmithDB ingestion, as a percentage of all write calls, over the selected time range.

**Why it matters:** Each failed call sends its task back for a retry. Failures that continue for about 2.5 hours lose runs.

**What to do:** Warning above 1%, critical above 5% with at least 50 failed calls.

**Tile:** Green: below 1%. Yellow: 1% or more. Red: 5% or more. Open the SmithDB ingestion section. Matches [Alert 5](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#5-writes-fail). For a monitor, use the same query over the last 15 minutes, and also require at least 50 failed calls.

definition.title: Query error rate, worst pool
definition.description:
**What it measures:** The highest share of failed queries of any SmithDB query pool, over the selected time range. Query error rate by pool shows which pool it is. Failures are the gRPC codes 2, 4, 8 (includes rejections), 13, 14, and 15, and the SmithDB statuses error and timeout. Client errors and cancellations are not included.

**Why it matters:** Users see these failures as errors in the UI and API. Each pool scales on its own, so one pool can fail while the others work.

**What to do:** Warning above 5%, critical above 10%. Open Failed queries by cause in the SmithDB query section: rejections, timeouts, and internal errors need different fixes.

**Tile:** Green: below 5%. Yellow: 5% or more. Red: 10% or more. Open the SmithDB query section. Matches [Alert 6](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#6-queries-fail). For a monitor, use the same query over the last 15 minutes, and alert for each pool.

definition.title: Pending compaction jobs
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Compaction jobs that wait for a compaction worker.

**Why it matters:** Compaction merges small segments. If it is late, queries become slower, and compaction applies deletes and retention late.

**What to do:** Short peaks are normal, for example after many deletes. A value that stays high for hours means that there are too few compaction workers. Add workers, or let KEDA scale them: set `smithdb.compactionWorker.autoscaling.keda.enabled: true` and `smithdb.compactionWorker.autoscaling.hpa.enabled: false`.

**Tile:** Green: below 1,000. Red: 1,000 or more. Open the SmithDB compaction section. Matches [Alert 10](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#10-compaction-falls-behind). For a monitor, alert when the value stays above 1,000 for the last 2 hours.

definition.title: Metastore connections, % of max
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Connections to the SmithDB metastore, as a percentage of max_connections. Select the database with the metastore variable, with the host tag of the Datadog PostgreSQL integration.

**Why it matters:** All SmithDB pods use connection pools to the metastore. When no connection is free, SmithDB writes and queries fail.

**What to do:** Warning above 80%, critical above 90%. Raise max_connections, or use a larger instance.

**Tile:** Green: below 80%. Yellow: 80% or more. Red: 90% or more. Open the SmithDB metastore (PostgreSQL) section. Matches [Alert 7](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#7-the-metastore-is-saturated). For a monitor, use the same query over the last 5 minutes.

**Requires:** The PostgreSQL integration.

definition.title: Redis memory, % of limit

formulas.formula: max(max(default_zero(100 * u / x), default_zero(e)), max(default_zero(100 * m), default_zero(100 * c))) / (u * 0 + e * 0 + m * 0 + c * 0 + 1)

definition.description:
**What it measures:** Memory use of the selected Redis, as a percentage of its limit. The tile takes the value of the provider that matches your selection: the Redis integration (used / maxmemory), ElastiCache, Memorystore, or Memorystore for Redis Cluster (fullest node).

**Why it matters:** Redis holds the ingestion queues and 6 hours of run data. With `volatile-lru`, the expected `maxmemory-policy`, Redis evicts keys that have an expiry time at the limit, such as run data, and runs can be lost.

**What to do:** Above 80% means that Redis will soon reach its limit. Drain the ingestion backlog, or give Redis more memory. Size Redis for your peak backlog, including periods when SmithDB writes are slow. No data: no Redis is selected with the redis variable, or its integration does not collect data.

**Tile:** Green: below 80%. Yellow: 80% or more. Red: 90% or more. Open the Redis section. Matches [Alert 4](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#4-redis-is-almost-full). For a monitor, use the same query over the last 10 minutes.

**Requires:** One of the Redis integration, the ElastiCache integration, the Memorystore integration, or the Memorystore for Redis Cluster integration.

definition.title: Fewest available pods in a SmithDB component
definition.description:
**What it measures:** The lowest number of available pods of any SmithDB Deployment. smithdb-migration is not included, because it normally has no pods.

**Why it matters:** A component without pods does not report metrics. Its charts then show no data instead of a problem.

**What to do:** 0 needs action: a component has no available pod. Open the Infrastructure block of each section to find the component, and examine its pod events.

**Tile:** Red: below 1. Green: 1 or more. Open the Infrastructure block of the component. Matches [Alert 12](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#12-a-component-has-no-pods). For a monitor, use the same query by kube_deployment over the last 10 minutes, and notify on no data.

**Requires:** The Datadog Kubernetes integration (kubelet and kube-state-metrics).

definition.title: Container restarts
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Container restarts of the SmithDB pods (all components except the migration) and the ingest queue workers during the selected time range. OOM kills are included.

**Why it matters:** A restart stops the work in progress. Restarts outside a rollout show crash loops, failed probes, or OOM kills.

**What to do:** Any restart outside a rollout needs action. 3 or more restarts of one pod in 30 minutes means a crash loop. The tile adds up the restarts of all pods during the selected time range. The alert counts each pod over 30 minutes, so a long time range can turn the tile red for restarts that are spread out.

**Tile:** Green: below 1. Yellow: 1 or more. Red: 3 or more. Open the Infrastructure block of each section. Matches [Alert 13](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#13-pods-restart-often). For a monitor, count the restarts of each pod over the last 30 minutes: warning at 1, critical at 3.

**Requires:** The Datadog Kubernetes integration (kubelet and kube-state-metrics). This tile shows 0, not No data, if the integration is missing.

definition.title: SmithDB panics

search.query: kube_deployment:*smithdb* (@backtrace:* OR "thread panicked") -"Runtime dropped task without completing it" $env $cluster $namespace

definition.description:
**What it measures:** SmithDB log lines for an unexpected internal error (a panic), during the selected time range. The count leaves out `Runtime dropped task without completing it`, which follows another failure in the same pod.

**Why it matters:** A panic is always a defect. A request fails, a background task stops, or the pod restarts. If the pod does not restart, no metric shows the panic.

**What to do:** Any value above 0 needs attention: open the log lines to see the component and the error. Examine the write errors, query errors, and container restarts of the same component.

**Tile:** Green: below 1. Yellow: 1 or more. Red: 4 or more. Open the Log Explorer with the same search. Matches [Alert 14](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#14-smithdb-panics). For a monitor, count the same log lines for each kube_deployment over the last 15 minutes: warning at 1, critical above 3.

**Requires:** SmithDB log collection. With JSON logs, parse them so that `backtrace` is a log attribute. Plain-text logs match on `thread panicked`.

definition.content: The work that reaches the system: runs and feedback that come in, and queries from users and automations. Use this section as context. A change in a backlog or in latency means more when you know whether the load changed. A sudden drop in runs stored while clients still send runs is an important alarm.

#### Writes
Runs and feedback that come in.

definition.title: Runs stored per second, over time
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Runs that SmithDB stored successfully per second.

**Why it matters:** This is the main load figure. Compare it with the tested ingestion rate of your SmithDB tier.

**What to do:** An increase means more queue length and latency soon. Scale before that happens. A drop while clients still send runs means that ingestion fails.

**Requires:** LangSmith metrics from the platform backend or the ingest queue (`langsmith_ingestion_e2e_latency_seconds`). The example Datadog configuration collects them.

definition.title: Feedback writes per second
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Feedback write requests that SmithDB receives per second.

**Why it matters:** Feedback uses the same ingest queue workers as runs, and adds load to the metastore. In some installations, most requests are feedback.

**What to do:** If feedback increases faster than runs, set `smithdb.mutations.enabled: true`, so that feedback uses its own query pods. Then examine the feedback retry backlog.

definition.content:
#### Reads
Queries from the UI, the API, and automations. The chart by type also shows feedback writes (`ingestfeedback`) and deletes (`deleteruns`). The other charts count reads only.

definition.title: Query requests per second, by pool
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Read requests to each SmithDB query pool per second. Feedback writes and deletes are not included.

**Why it matters:** Each pool scales independently. This shows which pool needs capacity.

**What to do:** If one pool increases, examine its latency, errors, and replicas in the SmithDB query section.

definition.title: Query requests per second, by type (top 10)
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Requests per second to the SmithDB query pools, for the 10 request types with the most requests. Each label is the gRPC path. The last part is the request type, for example `queryruns` (run lists), `querytrace` (trace view), `querythreads` (threads), `queryrunstats` (run statistics), `queryrunsforrunrulesstream` (automation rules), `ingestfeedback` (feedback writes), and `deleteruns` (deletes).

**Why it matters:** This shows which product feature creates the load on the query pools. One new automation rule or a dashboard with many statistics can double the load. Feedback writes and deletes also use these pools.

**What to do:** If a request type becomes the largest, find the feature that sends it. Many `queryrunsforrunrulesstream` requests come from automation rules. If `ingestfeedback` grows, examine the feedback retry backlog in the LangSmith ingestion section.

definition.content: These charts show runs and feedback that are lost, or that will be lost soon. **Evictions:** Redis keeps run data for 6 hours, also after ingestion. An eviction can remove data that SmithDB has not stored yet. **Failures by remaining attempts** show tasks that are close to their last attempt. **0 left** means lost. Failures with attempts left are a warning. Run tasks have 12 retries. Feedback mutation tasks have 25. `persist_batched_feedbacks` does not count all of its losses: see the tooltip of the feedback chart. **Dropped by project trace limit** is not a failure: LangSmith drops these runs on purpose when a project exceeds its monthly trace limit. Use it to explain missing traces. **Alerts:** [1](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#1-runs-are-lost), [2](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#2-feedback-is-lost).

definition.title: Redis evicted keys
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Keys that the selected Redis removed because its memory reached its limit. There is one line for each provider; only the line of your provider has data.

**Why it matters:** Redis keeps run payloads for 6 hours, also after ingestion. An eviction can remove a payload that SmithDB has not stored yet.

**What to do:** Normal is 0. Any eviction can mean lost runs. Give Redis more memory.

**Requires:** One of the Redis integration, the ElastiCache integration, the Memorystore integration, or the Memorystore for Redis Cluster integration.

definition.title: Run task failures by remaining attempts
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Failed attempts of run ingestion tasks in each interval, stacked by the number of attempts that are left: 3, 2, 1, or 0. Run tasks have 12 retries, so 0 left is attempt 12. Expected retries, such as rate limits, are not counted.

**Why it matters:** A task with attempts left is tried again. A failure with 0 left sends the task to the archive, and its runs are lost.

**What to do:** A failure with 0 left means data loss. Find the error in the logs of the ingest queue workers.

**Requires:** LangSmith metrics from the platform backend or the ingest queue (`langsmith_ingest_task_failures`). The example Datadog configuration collects them.

definition.title: Feedback task failures by remaining attempts
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Failed attempts of feedback tasks in each interval, stacked by the number of attempts that are left: 3, 2, 1, or 0. `persist_batched_feedbacks` has 12 retries, and the feedback mutation tasks have 25, so 0 left is attempt 12 or attempt 25. Expected retries are not counted. **`persist_batched_feedbacks` never shows 0 left:** it does not count failures while the run is not yet ingested, and reports failures only halfway and at 1 attempt left. If its last attempt fails, the feedback is lost, but this chart does not show it.

**Why it matters:** A task with attempts left is tried again. A failure with 0 left means that the feedback is lost.

**What to do:** A failure with 0 left means data loss. Find the error in the logs of the ingest queue workers. If feedback fails often, set `smithdb.mutations.enabled: true`.

**Requires:** LangSmith metrics from the platform backend or the ingest queue (`langsmith_ingest_task_failures`). The example Datadog configuration collects them.

definition.title: Runs dropped by project trace limit
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Runs that LangSmith dropped because their tracing project exceeded its monthly trace limit.

**Why it matters:** This loss comes from configuration, but users see it as missing traces.

**What to do:** Expected only if you set per-project trace limits. LangSmith drops these runs on purpose. If the values are unexpected, increase or remove the limit.

**Requires:** LangSmith metrics from the platform backend or the ingest queue (`langsmith_runs_dropped_per_project_limit`). The example Datadog configuration collects them.

definition.title: LangSmith ingestion (platform backend and ingest queue)

definition.content: The platform backend receives runs and puts them in Redis queues. Ingest queue workers take the tasks and write the runs to SmithDB. A backlog grows here before data expires: run data in Redis expires after 6 hours by default (Helm value `config.settings.redisRunsExpirySeconds`). If **Queue wait** increases and **Store write** stays stable, add ingest queue workers. If Store write increases, examine the SmithDB ingestion section. **Alerts:** [3](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#3-the-ingestion-backlog-gets-old), [13](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#13-pods-restart-often).

#### Service metrics
What the component reports about its own work: backlogs, latency, errors.

definition.title: Oldest waiting task by queue
definition.description:
**What it measures:** The age of the oldest waiting task in each ingestion and feedback queue.

**Why it matters:** Run data expires after 6 hours by default. This chart shows how close a queue is to that time.

**What to do:** Normal is less than a few seconds. The dashed lines are at 10 minutes (warning) and 30 minutes (critical). Above them, workers cannot process tasks as fast as they arrive. The thresholds apply to the ingestion queues.

**Requires:** LangSmith metrics from the platform backend or the ingest queue (`langsmith_asynq_queue_latency_seconds`). The example Datadog configuration collects them.

definition.title: Ingestion queue: pending vs retry
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Pending: tasks that no worker has started. Retry: tasks whose write failed and that wait for the next attempt.

**Why it matters:** A growing backlog shows a problem before latency and data loss increase.

**What to do:** Pending that grows while traffic is stable: too few workers, or SmithDB is slow. Retry that stays high: writes to SmithDB fail. The dashed lines are at 100 retries (warning) and 1,000 retries (critical, when the value stays above it for 30 minutes).

**Requires:** LangSmith metrics from the platform backend or the ingest queue (`langsmith_asynq_ingestion_queue_pending`, `langsmith_asynq_ingestion_queue_retry`). The example Datadog configuration collects them.

definition.title: Feedback queue: pending vs retry
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Feedback tasks that wait for a worker, and feedback tasks that wait for a retry.

**Why it matters:** Feedback retries use the same worker slots as run ingestion. A large feedback backlog makes run ingestion slower.

**What to do:** If the retry value stays high, set `smithdb.mutations.enabled: true`, so that feedback uses its own query pods.

**Requires:** LangSmith metrics from the platform backend or the ingest queue (`langsmith_asynq_feedback_queue_pending`, `langsmith_asynq_feedback_queue_retry`). The example Datadog configuration collects them.

definition.title: End-to-end ingestion latency p95
definition.description:
**What it measures:** For each run, the time from receipt by the platform backend to the SmithDB acknowledgement, including the wait in Redis and retries.

**Why it matters:** This is the ingestion delay that users see.

**What to do:** Normal is about 5 s. Short spikes are normal. If the value stays high, compare the oldest waiting task with SmithDB batch latency.

**Requires:** LangSmith metrics from the platform backend or the ingest queue (`langsmith_ingestion_e2e_latency_seconds`). The example Datadog configuration collects them.

definition.title: Queue wait vs store write p95
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Two parts of the end-to-end ingestion latency, for SmithDB. Queue wait: the time from when the platform backend received a run to when an ingest queue worker started its task. Store write: the time of one write call from the worker to SmithDB ingestion.

**Why it matters:** When end-to-end latency is high, this shows which step is slow: too few ingest queue workers, or a slow SmithDB.

**What to do:** Queue wait high while store write is stable: add ingest queue workers. Store write high: examine the SmithDB ingestion section. Normal in a large deployment: queue wait p95 0.2 s (busy hours up to 7 s), store write p95 3.8 s.

**Requires:** LangSmith metrics from the platform backend or the ingest queue (`langsmith_ingestion_api_to_worker_latency_seconds`, `langsmith_ingestion_worker_to_store_latency_seconds`). The example Datadog configuration collects them.

definition.content:
#### Infrastructure
Kubernetes signals of the component's pods: CPU use and throttling, memory use for the SmithDB data components, restarts and OOM kills, and replicas.

definition.title: Ingest path: CPU, % of limit, and throttling
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Left axis: CPU use of the fullest pod of each Deployment, as a percentage of its CPU limit. Right axis, orange: the share of CPU periods in which the pods were stopped at their CPU limit (throttling), across all pods. There is one line of each for every Deployment. No line means that the pods have no CPU limit.

**Why it matters:** The platform backend parses every run. Ingest queue workers decode and send every batch. Throttled pods process fewer tasks, and the queue grows. Throttling can occur below 100% CPU use, because short bursts hit the limit.

**What to do:** CPU above 80%, or throttling that increases, makes the ingestion queue grow. Add replicas, or raise the CPU limit. Ingest queue workers scale independently of SmithDB.

**Requires:** The Datadog Kubernetes integration (kubelet and kube-state-metrics).

definition.title: Ingest path: restarts and OOM kills

formulas.alias: Containers last stopped by OOM kill
Containers last stopped by OOM kill

definition.description:
**What it measures:** Left axis, orange: container restarts in each interval. Right axis: containers whose most recent stop was an OOM kill.

**Why it matters:** A restart stops the tasks in progress. They retry later, which adds delay and load.

**What to do:** Any restart outside a rollout needs action. Read the logs of the previous container. OOM kills mean that the memory limit is too low.

**Requires:** The Datadog Kubernetes integration (kubelet and kube-state-metrics).

definition.title: Ingest path: autoscaler use and unavailable replicas
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Left axis: current replicas of each autoscaler, as a percentage of its maximum replicas. 100% means that it cannot add more pods. Right axis, orange: replicas that should run but are not available; they stay at 0 when all pods run.

**Why it matters:** Ingest queue workers scale independently of SmithDB, with an HPA or KEDA on queue length. At the autoscaler maximum, the queue grows when traffic grows.

**What to do:** Current replicas at the maximum for a long time: raise the maximum, if SmithDB ingestion has capacity. Available below desired: pods cannot start; examine the pod events.

**Requires:** The Datadog Kubernetes integration (kubelet and kube-state-metrics).

definition.content: SmithDB ingestion keeps runs in memory for a short time. Then it writes them to object storage as segments (data files), and records the metadata of each segment in the metastore. If batch latency is high, examine the Object storage and SmithDB metastore sections. **Alerts:** [5](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#5-writes-fail), [8](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#8-writes-are-slow), [12](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#12-a-component-has-no-pods), [13](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#13-pods-restart-often).

#### Service metrics
What the component reports about its own work: backlogs, latency, errors.

definition.title: SmithDB batch latency and flush failures
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Left axis: the time that SmithDB ingestion needs to save the runs of one partition (one project on one day) in object storage and the metastore (p50 and p99). Right axis, orange line: flushes to object storage that failed in each interval. The orange line stays at 0 when no flush fails. If it is missing, the metric is not collected.

**Why it matters:** This is the time of the store write step of ingestion. If it increases, store write in the LangSmith ingestion section increases too.

**What to do:** Normal p50 is about 0.5 to 0.7 s. p50 above 1.6 s (warning) or 2 s (critical) for 15 minutes: flushes are slow; examine object storage and metastore latency. Failures at a steady rate: object storage or the metastore returns errors.

definition.title: SmithDB write error rate
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Failed write calls to SmithDB ingestion (gRPC status other than 0, including cancellations), as a percentage of all write calls.

**Why it matters:** This is the most direct sign that SmithDB rejects writes. Each failed call sends its task back for a retry; after about 2.5 hours of retries, the runs are lost. The retry queue shows the same problem only later.

**What to do:** Normal is close to 0%. Warning above 1%, critical above 5% with at least 50 failed calls, sustained for 15 minutes. Find the error in the ingest queue and SmithDB ingestion logs; Unavailable errors often come from a proxy or service mesh between the pods.

definition.content:
#### Infrastructure
Kubernetes signals of the component's pods: CPU use and throttling, memory use for the SmithDB data components, restarts and OOM kills, and replicas.

definition.title: SmithDB ingestion: CPU, % of limit, and throttling
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Left axis: CPU use of the fullest pod of each Deployment, as a percentage of its CPU limit. Right axis, orange: the share of CPU periods in which the pods were stopped at their CPU limit (throttling), across all pods. There is one line of each for every Deployment. No line means that the pods have no CPU limit.

**Why it matters:** Ingestion sorts, encodes, and compresses every segment. Throttling makes flushes slower. Throttling can occur below 100% CPU use, because short bursts hit the limit.

**What to do:** CPU above 80%, or throttling that increases, while batch latency increases: raise the CPU limit or add replicas.

**Requires:** The Datadog Kubernetes integration (kubelet and kube-state-metrics).

definition.title: SmithDB ingestion: memory, % of limit (fullest pod)
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Memory of the fullest pod of each Deployment, as a percentage of its memory limit: the highest working set of its pods, divided by the memory limit. All pods of a Deployment have the same limit.

**Why it matters:** Ingestion pods hold runs in memory until they write them to object storage. A pod that reaches its limit is stopped (OOM kill), and the writes that it holds fail and retry.

**What to do:** Above 80%, the pod gets near an OOM kill. Examine the batch latency and flush failures, then add replicas or memory.

**Requires:** The Datadog Kubernetes integration (kubelet and kube-state-metrics).

definition.title: SmithDB ingestion: restarts and OOM kills

formulas.alias: Containers last stopped by OOM kill

definition.description:
**What it measures:** Left axis, orange: container restarts in each interval. Right axis: containers whose most recent stop was an OOM kill.

**Why it matters:** A restart drops the rows that were not flushed. Their tasks retry from Redis, so no data is lost, but ingestion is delayed.

**What to do:** Any restart outside a rollout needs action. Read the logs of the previous container. OOM kills mean that the memory limit is too low.

**Requires:** The Datadog Kubernetes integration (kubelet and kube-state-metrics).

definition.title: SmithDB ingestion: autoscaler use and unavailable replicas
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Left axis: current replicas of each autoscaler, as a percentage of its maximum replicas. 100% means that it cannot add more pods. Right axis, orange: replicas that should run but are not available; they stay at 0 when all pods run.

**Why it matters:** The ingestion HPA scales on CPU. At the maximum, SmithDB ingestion cannot take more load.

**What to do:** Current replicas at the maximum for a long time: raise the maximum or set a larger `smithdb.resourceTier`. Available below desired: pods cannot start; run `kubectl describe pod`, and make sure that the cache PersistentVolumeClaim is Bound.

**Requires:** The Datadog Kubernetes integration (kubelet and kube-state-metrics).

definition.content: The SmithDB query pools serve the reads of the UI, the API, and automations. The mutations pool also writes feedback and deletes runs. Rejected queries fail for users. An admission rejection means that a query pod is out of memory. A fanout rejection means that compaction is late, or that the time range is too wide. A fanout that increases shows early that compaction is late. Each pool (query, stats-query, run-rules, mutations) scales independently. **Alerts:** [6](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#6-queries-fail), [9](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#9-queries-are-slow), [12](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#12-a-component-has-no-pods), [13](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#13-pods-restart-often).

#### Service metrics
What the component reports about its own work: backlogs, latency, errors.

definition.title: Query latency p95 by pool
definition.description:
**What it measures:** The p95 duration of requests to each SmithDB query pool. Feedback writes and run deletes are not included.

**Why it matters:** This is the read speed that users see in the UI and API. Slow queries usually come before failed queries.

**What to do:** Warning above 10 s, critical above 20 s, for 15 minutes. Examine the scan fanout, the admission queue, and the pending compaction jobs.

definition.title: Query error rate by pool
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Server-side failures of the calls to each pool, as a percentage of all calls. Server-side failures are the gRPC codes 2 (unknown), 4 (deadline exceeded), 8 (resource exhausted), 13 (internal), 14 (unavailable), and 15 (data loss), and the SmithDB statuses error and timeout. Client errors and cancellations are not included.

**Why it matters:** Users see these failures as errors in the UI and API. The mutations pool also returns code 9 when feedback arrives before its run. That is expected, and LangSmith retries it, so the chart does not count it.

**What to do:** Warning above 5%, critical above 10%, for 15 minutes. Examine Failed queries by cause, and the Object storage and SmithDB metastore sections.

definition.title: Failed queries by cause
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Queries that SmithDB stopped: admission queue full, fanout limit exceeded, or an operation over its memory limit.

**Why it matters:** Each cause has a different fix.

**What to do:** Admission queue full: add replicas or memory. Fanout limit: compaction is late. Memory limit: a few are normal; a steady increase means queries need more memory.

**Requires:** SmithDB metrics mode `all` for `operation_memory_limit_exceeded`. The Helm chart sets `SMITHDB_<COMPONENT>__METRICS__MODE` to `critical` by default. Set it to `all`, for example in `smithdb.commonEnv`.

definition.title: Admission queue length by pool
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Requests that wait because the memory of a query pod is at its limit.

**Why it matters:** Waiting requests are slow. When the queue is full (100 requests by default, set with `SMITHDB_QUERY__QUERY_ADMISSION_QUEUE_SIZE`), SmithDB rejects new requests.

**What to do:** Normal is 0. A value above 0 for a long time means that the pool needs more replicas or memory.

definition.title: Scan fanout p99
definition.description:
**What it measures:** The number of scan partitions that one query must open. A scan partition is approximately one segment or a group of segments. 99% of queries open this number or fewer.

**Why it matters:** More scan partitions make queries slower and use more memory. Above 10,000 scan partitions, SmithDB rejects the query.

**What to do:** A rising trend while traffic is stable means that compaction is behind. Examine the SmithDB compaction section.

definition.content:
#### Infrastructure
Kubernetes signals of the component's pods: CPU use and throttling, memory use for the SmithDB data components, restarts and OOM kills, and replicas.

definition.title: Query pools: CPU, % of limit, and throttling
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Left axis: CPU use of the fullest pod of each Deployment, as a percentage of its CPU limit. Right axis, orange: the share of CPU periods in which the pods were stopped at their CPU limit (throttling), across all pods. There is one line of each for every Deployment. No line means that the pods have no CPU limit.

**Why it matters:** Queries decode, filter, and merge segments. Throttling shows as query latency. Throttling can occur below 100% CPU use, because short bursts hit the limit.

**What to do:** CPU above 80%, or throttling that increases, while query latency increases: raise the CPU limit or add replicas to that pool.

**Requires:** The Datadog Kubernetes integration (kubelet and kube-state-metrics).

definition.title: Query pools: memory, % of limit (fullest pod)
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Memory of the fullest pod of each Deployment, as a percentage of its memory limit: the highest working set of its pods, divided by the memory limit. All pods of a Deployment have the same limit.

**Why it matters:** Query pods usually run out of memory before they run out of CPU. Near the limit, requests wait in the admission queue or SmithDB rejects them. An autoscaler that uses CPU does not add replicas in this case.

**What to do:** Above 80%, add replicas or memory to that pool, or set a minimum replica count that holds your normal load. Examine the admission queue in the SmithDB query section.

**Requires:** The Datadog Kubernetes integration (kubelet and kube-state-metrics).

definition.title: Query pools: restarts and OOM kills

formulas.alias: Containers last stopped by OOM kill
Containers last stopped by OOM kill
Containers last stopped by OOM kill

definition.description:
**What it measures:** Left axis, orange: container restarts in each interval. Right axis: containers whose most recent stop was an OOM kill.

**Why it matters:** A restart fails the queries in progress and empties the pod's memory cache.

**What to do:** Any restart outside a rollout needs action. OOM kills mean that the pool needs more memory or more replicas.

**Requires:** The Datadog Kubernetes integration (kubelet and kube-state-metrics).

definition.title: Query pools: autoscaler use and unavailable replicas
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Left axis: current replicas of each autoscaler, as a percentage of its maximum replicas. 100% means that it cannot add more pods. Right axis, orange: replicas that should run but are not available; they stay at 0 when all pods run.

**Why it matters:** Each query pool (query, stats-query, run-rules, mutations) has its own autoscaler. At the maximum, a pool cannot add capacity.

**What to do:** Current replicas at the maximum for a long time: raise the maximum for that pool. Available below desired: pods cannot start; run `kubectl describe pod`, and make sure that the cache PersistentVolumeClaim is Bound.

**Requires:** The Datadog Kubernetes integration (kubelet and kube-state-metrics).

definition.content: Compaction merges small segments into larger segments, and applies deletes and retention. If compaction is late, queries become slower and storage grows. If running jobs stay at 0 while jobs are pending, compaction has stopped. If pending jobs stay high for hours, there are too few workers. **Alerts:** [10](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#10-compaction-falls-behind), [11](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#11-compaction-stops-or-fails), [12](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#12-a-component-has-no-pods), [13](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#13-pods-restart-often).

#### Service metrics
What the component reports about its own work: backlogs, latency, errors.

definition.title: Compaction jobs: pending vs running
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Pending: jobs that wait for a compaction worker. Running: jobs that workers run now.

**Why it matters:** Running jobs at 0 while jobs are pending means that compaction has stopped.

**What to do:** Pending that stays high for hours: too few workers. Running at 0 with pending jobs: check that workers can connect to the compaction scheduler. The dashed line is at 1,000 pending jobs (critical, when the value stays above it for 2 hours).

definition.title: Compaction failure rate by job kind
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Failed compaction jobs, as a percentage of all completed jobs, for each compaction job kind (`*_compaction`). Data flush and publisher jobs are not included.

**Why it matters:** One job kind can break while the others work.

**What to do:** Normal is well under 2%. Warning above 20%, critical above 50%, over 1 hour. A job kind with failures and no successes does not work. Find the error in the compaction worker logs.

definition.content:
#### Infrastructure: compaction workers
Kubernetes signals of the worker pods: CPU use and throttling, memory use, restarts and OOM kills, and replicas.

definition.title: Compaction workers: CPU, % of limit, and throttling
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Left axis: CPU use of the fullest pod of each Deployment, as a percentage of its CPU limit. Right axis, orange: the share of CPU periods in which the pods were stopped at their CPU limit (throttling), across all pods. There is one line of each for every Deployment. No line means that the pods have no CPU limit.

**Why it matters:** Compaction decodes, merges, and encodes segments. Throttled workers finish fewer jobs. Throttling can occur below 100% CPU use, because short bursts hit the limit.

**What to do:** CPU above 80%, or throttling that increases, while pending jobs grow: raise the CPU limit or add workers.

**Requires:** The Datadog Kubernetes integration (kubelet and kube-state-metrics).

definition.title: Compaction workers: memory, % of limit (fullest pod)
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Memory of the fullest pod of each Deployment, as a percentage of its memory limit: the highest working set of its pods, divided by the memory limit. All pods of a Deployment have the same limit.

**Why it matters:** Large compaction jobs need much memory. A worker that reaches its limit is stopped (OOM kill), and its running jobs fail and are planned again.

**What to do:** Above 80%, give the workers more memory, so that large jobs fit. If one job kind fails again and again, examine the compaction failure rate by job kind.

**Requires:** The Datadog Kubernetes integration (kubelet and kube-state-metrics).

definition.title: Compaction workers: restarts and OOM kills

formulas.alias: Containers last stopped by OOM kill

definition.description:
**What it measures:** Left axis, orange: container restarts in each interval. Right axis: containers whose most recent stop was an OOM kill.

**Why it matters:** A restart fails the jobs that the worker runs. The scheduler plans them again.

**What to do:** Any restart outside a rollout needs action. OOM kills mean that jobs are too large for the memory limit.

**Requires:** The Datadog Kubernetes integration (kubelet and kube-state-metrics).

definition.title: Compaction workers: autoscaler use and unavailable replicas
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Left axis: current replicas of each autoscaler, as a percentage of its maximum replicas. 100% means that it cannot add more pods. Right axis, orange: replicas that should run but are not available; they stay at 0 when all pods run.

**Why it matters:** Compaction workers scale on CPU (HPA) or on pending jobs (KEDA). At the maximum, pending jobs grow.

**What to do:** Current replicas at the maximum with pending jobs that grow: raise the maximum. Available below desired: pods cannot start; check their cache volumes.

**Requires:** The Datadog Kubernetes integration (kubelet and kube-state-metrics).

definition.content: The cluster manager sends the runs of one project to the same ingestion pod, and the queries of one workspace to the same query pod. If it is not available, requests go to any pod. Nothing fails, but load increases. **Alerts:** [12](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#12-a-component-has-no-pods), [13](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#13-pods-restart-often).

#### Infrastructure
Kubernetes signals of the component's pods: CPU use and throttling, memory use for the SmithDB data components, restarts and OOM kills, and replicas.

definition.title: Cluster manager: CPU, % of limit, and throttling
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Left axis: CPU use of the fullest pod of each Deployment, as a percentage of its CPU limit. Right axis, orange: the share of CPU periods in which the pods were stopped at their CPU limit (throttling), across all pods. There is one line of each for every Deployment. No line means that the pods have no CPU limit.

**Why it matters:** The cluster manager recomputes assignments when pods change or load moves. Throttling can occur below 100% CPU use, because short bursts hit the limit.

**What to do:** CPU above 80%, or throttling that increases, delays the assignments of projects and workspaces to pods. Raise the CPU limit.

**Requires:** The Datadog Kubernetes integration (kubelet and kube-state-metrics).

definition.title: Cluster manager: restarts and OOM kills

formulas.alias: Containers last stopped by OOM kill

definition.description:
**What it measures:** Left axis, orange: container restarts in each interval. Right axis: containers whose most recent stop was an OOM kill.

**Why it matters:** While the cluster manager restarts, requests go to any pod. Ingestion writes smaller segments, and query caches work less well.

**What to do:** Any restart outside a rollout needs action. Read the logs of the previous container.

**Requires:** The Datadog Kubernetes integration (kubelet and kube-state-metrics).

definition.title: Cluster manager: replicas
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Desired and available replicas of the cluster manager.

**Why it matters:** Without an available replica, SmithDB routes requests to any pod.

**What to do:** Available below desired: the pod cannot start; examine the pod events.

**Requires:** The Datadog Kubernetes integration (kubelet and kube-state-metrics).

definition.content: Redis holds the ingestion queues and 6 hours of run data. The expected `maxmemory-policy` is `volatile-lru`: when memory reaches `maxmemory`, Redis evicts keys that have an expiry time, such as run data, and runs can be lost. Select your Redis with the **redis** variable, for example `cluster_id:<name>` (Memorystore for Redis Cluster), `cacheclusterid:<node>` (ElastiCache), `instance_id:<id>` (Memorystore), or `redis_host:<host>` (Datadog Redis integration). **Alerts:** [1](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#1-runs-are-lost), [4](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#4-redis-is-almost-full).

definition.title: Redis memory, % of limit
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Memory use of the selected Redis, as a percentage of its limit. There is one line for each provider; only the line of your provider has data: the Redis integration (used / maxmemory), ElastiCache, Memorystore, or Memorystore for Redis Cluster (fullest node).

**Why it matters:** Redis holds the ingestion queues and 6 hours of run data. With `volatile-lru`, the expected `maxmemory-policy`, Redis evicts keys that have an expiry time at the limit, such as run data, and runs can be lost.

**What to do:** Warning above 80%, critical above 90%, for 10 minutes. Drain the ingestion backlog, or give Redis more memory. If the Redis integration line is missing, `maxmemory` is not set.

**Requires:** One of the Redis integration, the ElastiCache integration, the Memorystore integration, or the Memorystore for Redis Cluster integration.

definition.title: Redis CPU

formulas.alias: Memorystore Cluster, % of node CPU (busiest node)

definition.description:
**What it measures:** CPU use of Redis. Memorystore: percentage of one core. ElastiCache: engine CPU. Memorystore for Redis Cluster: CPU of the busiest node.

**Why it matters:** Redis runs commands on one main thread. Above one core, it cannot do more work.

**What to do:** Warning above 90% of one core (0.9 cores), sustained. All Redis operations then become slower. Use a larger Redis instance.

**Requires:** The ElastiCache, Memorystore, or Memorystore for Redis Cluster integration.

definition.title: LangSmith Redis client errors
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Redis errors that LangSmith services see: timeouts, network errors, and server errors.

**Why it matters:** This is the Redis health that LangSmith sees.

**What to do:** More timeouts mean that Redis is overloaded. Examine Redis CPU and memory.

**Requires:** LangSmith metrics from the platform backend or the ingest queue (`langsmith_redis_errors`). The example Datadog configuration collects them.

definition.content: The metastore records the metadata of every segment that SmithDB writes, and stores new feedback until compaction moves it. If it is slow, ingestion becomes slower. If connections or storage run out, SmithDB writes fail. Select your database with the **metastore** variable, for example `dbclusteridentifier:<name>` (Aurora), `dbinstanceidentifier:<name>` (RDS), `database_id:<project>:<name>` (Cloud SQL), `cluster_id:<name>` (AlloyDB), `name:<server>` (Azure Database for PostgreSQL), or `host:<host>` (Datadog PostgreSQL integration). On Google Cloud, the PostgreSQL integration does not add the `database_id` or `cluster_id` tag. Add the tag to the `tags` of the PostgreSQL check, so that the % of max_connections line and the Metastore connections, % of max tile also show data. **Alerts:** [7](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-alerts#7-the-metastore-is-saturated).

definition.title: Metastore connections
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Connections to the SmithDB metastore. Left axis: % of max_connections (PostgreSQL integration). Right axis, orange: the connection count from RDS, Cloud SQL, AlloyDB, or Azure.

**Why it matters:** All SmithDB pods use connection pools. When no connection is free, SmithDB writes and queries fail.

**What to do:** Warning above 80%, critical above 90% of max_connections. Raise max_connections, or use a larger instance.

**Requires:** One of the PostgreSQL integration, the RDS integration, the Cloud SQL integration, the AlloyDB metrics of the Google Cloud integration, or the Azure Database for PostgreSQL integration.

definition.title: Metastore CPU
definition.description:
**What it measures:** CPU use of the SmithDB metastore instance.

**Why it matters:** A busy metastore makes flushes and queries slower.

**What to do:** Warning above 60%, critical above 80%, for 15 minutes. Look for slow queries, then use a larger instance.

**Requires:** One of the RDS integration, the Cloud SQL integration, the AlloyDB metrics of the Google Cloud integration, or the Azure Database for PostgreSQL integration.

definition.title: Metastore memory
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Memory of the SmithDB metastore instance. Left axis: free memory (RDS) or available memory (AlloyDB), in bytes. Right axis, orange: used memory, in % (Cloud SQL, Azure).

**Why it matters:** Low free memory means fewer cached pages and slower reads and writes.

**What to do:** Free memory near 0, or used memory near 100%: use an instance with more memory. No alert uses this chart. It helps to explain a slow metastore.

**Requires:** One of the RDS integration, the Cloud SQL integration, the AlloyDB metrics of the Google Cloud integration, or the Azure Database for PostgreSQL integration.

definition.title: Metastore storage
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Storage of the SmithDB metastore. Left axis: storage used, in % (Cloud SQL, Azure), with the 85% critical line. Right axis, orange: free storage (RDS, Aurora local storage), cluster volume used (Aurora), or storage used (AlloyDB), in bytes.

**Why it matters:** Feedback stays in the metastore until compaction moves it. A full disk stops all SmithDB writes.

**What to do:** Critical: more than 85% used (Cloud SQL, Azure), or less than 10 GiB free (RDS; adjust to your volume). Do not alert on Aurora and AlloyDB if their storage increases automatically. Fast growth: make sure that compaction is not late.

**Requires:** One of the RDS integration, the Cloud SQL integration, the AlloyDB metrics of the Google Cloud integration, or the Azure Database for PostgreSQL integration.

definition.content: Durable storage for SmithDB. Put errors make flushes fail, and tasks retry. Get errors make queries fail. A low, steady rate of get errors can be normal. Act on changes.

definition.title: Object storage error rate by operation
definition.description:
**What it measures:** Failed object storage calls, as a percentage of all calls, for each operation.

**Why it matters:** Put errors make flushes fail and tasks retry. Get errors make queries fail.

**What to do:** A low, steady rate of get errors can be normal. Act on an increase, and on any steady rate of put errors.

definition.title: Object storage latency p99 by operation
definition.description:
**What it measures:** The p99 duration of object storage calls, for each operation.

**Why it matters:** Every flush, compaction job, and cache miss waits for object storage. Normal p99 in a large deployment: get about 0.2 s, put about 0.25 s, multipart put about 30 s.

**What to do:** If flush duration or query latency increases, examine this chart first. Check the bucket region and network.
